# Tlāloc and the industries that were always telling its story
Archetypes are not metaphors; they are job descriptions written early. **Tlāloc**'s was unusually clear.

Tlāloc's myths turn on a single terrifying truth: the same rain that feeds can also drown, strike, or rot. He is generous and punitive in equal measure.

The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) — which maps every flagship temple to the industries its archetype demonstrably resonates with, each match argued and open to challenge — seats this temple in **3 industries**. This file reads those seats the way they were earned: through the myths.
## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Tlāloc
- **Pantheon:** Nahuatl
- **Domain of influence:** Rain, Water, Lightning
- **Pattern seats:** 3
- **Sectors touched:** Energy & Natural World
- **Strongest seat:** Agriculture, Food & Harvest
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 244 of 271
## The Myth at Work

**The Abduction of Xōchiquetzal.** Colonial accounts make Xōchiquetzal, the young goddess of flowers, weaving, and sexual love, the wife of Tlāloc before Tezcatlipoca abducted her for her beauty (Leyenda de los Soles).  The tradition bound the green growing world to the water that sustains it. — hold that image; the industries below are where it goes to work.

**The Destruction of the Fourth Sun.** The Fourth Sun, the Sun of Water (4-Water), was ruled by Tlāloc's consort Chalchiuhtlicue, and it ended in a flood that lasted fifty-two years.  Humans were transformed into fish; the cosmos had to be remade. — hold that image; the industries below are where it goes to work.
## The Seats

Each of these is argued in the atlas with a weight and a why-line. What the atlas cannot fit in one line is the whole myth — so here is each seat with its story restored.

### Agriculture, Food & Harvest

*Farming, grain, food production, and agtech. (Sector: Energy & Natural World)*

*Rain decides the harvest; the most propitiated farmer’s god of Mesoamerica.* — the atlas stops there, out of discipline. The myth keeps going: the function Tlāloc performs in the stories is precisely the function this industry sells.

### Meteorology & Weather Intelligence

*Forecasting, storm tracking, and climate analytics. (Sector: Energy & Natural World)*

The why-line says it in one breath: *Rain and lightning together; the agricultural forecast made divine.* That is not a resemblance; it is the same act, performed in a newer building.

### Freshwater & Hydrology

*Water supply, irrigation, and watershed management. (Sector: Energy & Natural World)*

The why-line says it in one breath: *Rain is the supply side of every water system.* That is not a resemblance; it is the same act, performed in a newer building.

Read the myth again after the seats and it stops sounding ancient: Tlāloc's myths turn on a single terrifying truth: the same rain that feeds can also drown, strike, or rot. The age changed. The work did not.
## The Method, Stated Plainly

None of this is numerology. A seat exists only where the match can be argued from the deity's documented domains and deeds — weighted, published, and falsifiable. If you work in agriculture, food & harvest, meteorology & weather intelligence, or any trade this temple holds a seat in, this is the honest version of what a placement means: your industry beside the story it has been re-telling all along — on the temple floor itself, before an audience that came specifically to read it. The [patron tier](/sites/tlaloc/patron/) and the [advertising terms](/terms/advertising/) describe the mechanics; the resonance above describes the fit. The story is the pitch; the seats are just where it already works.
